findings.title: Fabrication charge and the public composition test
findings.claim: The focus's fabrication allegation is a rival account of how the revealed discourse was made, set against al-haqq as truth and—by a bounded construction image—as coherent speech. The repeated challenge to produce comparable surahs in 10:38 and 11:13 makes that authorship dispute a public test; 16:105 supplies a reversed mirror by naming disbelievers in God's signs as fabricators.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb carries both the ordinary false-fabrication charge and a metaphorical make/cut image; the truth predicate supplies its contrast. The exact external accusations and comparable-surah challenges contact that fabrication carrier, while the speech-construction specialization contacts the same challenge. The 16:105 connection reverses the accusation's direction without proving that every speaker in the passages is the same.
findings.reader_payoff: The dispute becomes perceptible as a question of provenance and construction, not only a disagreement over a proposition: the accusation is repeated, put to comparison, and mirrored by a later counter-accusation.
findings.containment: The focus rebuttal remains intact, and neither side is ranked. The cut-to-make image is metaphorical pressure, not literal cutting; F002's speech-construction specialization is accompanied by its F001 material core. The connection records give exact target Arabic but no target morphology, so no target-side lexical analysis or identity between the accused groups is asserted.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run anchor and two legacy reader-walk records converge on focus branches; the cross-surah connections supply exact Arabic and stated relations but explicitly lack target morphology.
